faq.a: Abdi is associated with the Arabic form عَبْدِي, whose core sense is abdi; my servant (of god).

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdi?
faq.a: Abdi is associated with Arabic. Abdi is Arabic عَبْدِي (ʿAbdī), meaning 'my servant', used as a male given name especially in the Horn of Africa.
Yes — the underlying form عَبْدِي is Arabic.
Abdi can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abdi should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ع ب د is Quranic, but ʿAbd is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Abdi mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Abdi is rendered عبدی and carries the sense عبدی، میرا بندہ.

faq.q: What does Abdi mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Abdi is rendered عبدی and carries the sense عبدی، بنده من.
A romanized syllable approximation is ab-di. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Abdi?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Abdi, abdi. Script forms are عبدي, عبدی, عَبْدِي, अब्दी.

faq.q: Is Abdi a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
